The Engineering Design Notebook — your whole-year tool

Not just some pages — a system. One bound composition book each student keeps and uses every class day, all year: bellwork, notes, sketches, vocabulary, exit tickets, and project logs all live inside it. Graded on a rubric every two weeks, and it is how they study for their certification — same setup in both classes, so you run one routine.

Where vocabulary goes — and how

Back of the book (pp. 181–200). Four columns, English + Spanish, always with a sketch — consistent and review-ready for the certification:

Term (EN / ES)Meaning (my words)SketchSentence
prototype / prototipoa first model you build to test an idea✏️"We built a cardboard prototype first."
tolerance / toleranciahow much a size is allowed to be off✏️"The tolerance was ±1 mm."

Cognates (diseño, material, estructura, prototipo) are flagged so Spanish speakers get instant footholds.

Notebook check — 20 pts, every 2 weeks

Completeness — all class days present5
Dated entries (date + entry # + page)3
Table of Contents kept current3
Vocabulary (all 4 columns filled)4
Sketches present & labeled3
Neatness & pen/pencil convention2

Fast check (< 1 min/book): "open to entry #7, your best sketch, and today," then verify 2 random ToC lines. Stamp the glued-in rubric.

Day-1 setup (fits 45 minutes)

  1. Name on the cover and spine.
  2. Glue the Notebook Map + rubric to the inside cover.
  3. p.1 Title Page — Engineering Design Notebook · name · class · period · 2026–27.
  4. p.2 About the Engineer — finish the sentences + draw your logo.
  5. pp.3–6 Table of Contents — rule 4 columns: # | Date | Topic | Page.
  6. p.7 copy the 5 rules; p.8 glue the rubric + check log.
  7. Number pages 1–8; flip to the back, label p.177 Reference and p.181 Vocabulary Bank (rule the 4 vocab columns).
  8. Write your first ToC line: "Notebook Setup — p.1."

The 5 rules (a real engineer's record)

  1. Write in blue/black pen. Sketch in pencil.
  2. Date every entry.
  3. Mistakes: one line through + initials. Never scribble, white-out, or tear out a page.
  4. Number every page and add it to the Table of Contents.
  5. Neat enough that someone else could repeat your work.

Why: an engineer's notebook is a dated record of what you did and when — that is why you never tear out a page.

Principles — Week 1
Day 1 — Welcome + Procedures + Notebook
Welcome to Engineering! Today: how our class runs and the syllabus, then you set up your Engineering Design Notebook.
Bring this week: one bound composition book.
Turn in: nothing today — just your notebook set up (name, table of contents, first entry).
Day 2 — What Is Engineering?
Watch the video, fill in the guided-viewing sheet, then sketch and label one engineered object you can see in the room.
Turn in: your guided-viewing sheet + labeled sketch.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=btGYcizV0iI
Day 3 — Paper Airplane Challenge
The engineering design process. In your team: Ask → Imagine → Plan → Create → Improve a paper airplane (1 sheet, folds only, 2 throws). Record every step.
Turn in: your Design-Process Record Sheet.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MAhpfFt_mWM
Day 4 — Paper Tower Challenge
Build the tallest free-standing tower from 5 sheets (folds/rolls only — must stand on its own for 10 seconds). You get two builds; improve between them.
Turn in: your Tower Iteration Reflection.
Day 5 — Types of Engineering + Quiz Game
Match products to their branch of engineering (team quiz), then a quick hunt for engineering around campus/the room.
Turn in: your 'Spot the Engineering' sheet (3 things: what it is, its branch, the problem it solves).
Principles — Week 2
Day 6 — Build-a-Car: Plan & Design
Plan your rolling car on paper FIRST — sketch it and list materials (body, axles/straws, wheels). No building yet.
Turn in: your Car Planning Sheet with sketch, materials list, and distance prediction.
Day 7 — Build Day
Build your car from your approved plan. Straws = axles; wheels must spin freely; keep the axles parallel so it rolls straight. Roll-test as you go.
Turn in: nothing — get it built and note one fix for test day.
Day 8 — Test, Measure, Improve
Ramp test: two trials, release (no push), measure the distance. Make ONE improvement between runs.
Turn in: your Test & Improve Data Sheet.
Day 9 — The Real Tool: Fusion 360
Watch the Fusion 360 intro, then make sure you can log into your school email IN CLASS — we create your Autodesk account next class.
Turn in: your Account-Setup email card.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Izh99EnGLGw
Day 10 — Create Account + Launch Fusion
Create your Autodesk education account with your school email (link below), verify it, then open Fusion 360 and save a file named yourname-test.
Turn in: your Fusion First-Look Checklist.
Autodesk student sign-up: https://www.autodesk.com/education/edu-software/overview  (choose Fusion)
Manufacturing — Week 1
Day 1 — Welcome Back + Shop Safety + Notebook
Welcome back to Manufacturing! Today: how the shop runs, the lab-safety non-negotiables, and a quick Year-2 notebook setup.
Bring: a new bound composition book.
Turn in: your signed Lab-Safety Agreement + notebook set up.
Day 2 — Manufacturing Systems
Watch the production-line video + take notes, then do the vocabulary match and the job/batch/continuous scenario sort.
Turn in: your Manufacturing Systems worksheet.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9hD24pOXsAo
Day 3 — Planning & Logistics
Learn JIT, bottleneck, supply chain, and cycle time, then map the workflow of a simple product and circle the bottleneck.
Turn in: your Logistics Vocabulary + Workflow Diagram.
Day 4 — The Industry, Careers & Safety
Watch the factory tour, pick a manufacturing career for your one-pager, and see how a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) works.
Turn in: your Manufacturing Career one-pager.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=77UMEc7ZKJE
Day 5 — Design a Product Worth Making
Use the design process (Ask → Research → Brainstorm) to define a real problem and sketch three ideas — this becomes your first Fusion project.
Turn in: your 'Develop Your Own Product Idea' sheet.
Manufacturing — Week 2
Day 6 — Measure Like a Machinist
Learn the caliper and speed square, and precision vs. tolerance, then measure objects at the stations and record to the nearest tenth.
Turn in: your Measuring Lab data sheet.
Day 7 — Manufacturing Math
Conversions (inches ↔ mm), fractions/decimals, and tolerance ranges — tied to real part dimensions.
Turn in: your Manufacturing Math practice sheet.
Day 8 — Parametric Design in Fusion
Watch the Fusion refresher, then build a plate driven by parameters (width, height, thickness) and change one value to watch it update.
Turn in: your 3 parameters written in your notebook (name = value + what each controls).
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Izh99EnGLGw
Day 9 — Start the Parametric Project (Mounting Plate)
Plan your plate's dimensions and hole spacing on the planning sheet, then begin modeling it parametrically in Fusion.
Turn in: your Part Planning Sheet + start your Fusion file (yourname-plate).
Day 10 — Continue + Certification Kickoff
Keep building your plate, and learn the Autodesk certification path (the 5 exam domains) we're working toward all year.
Turn in: your Certification Path self-check + your progress on the plate.

Fusion Project Bank → Autodesk Certification

The certification: Autodesk Certified User (ACU): Autodesk Fusion

Format: 35-40 selected-response items · 50 minutes · target ~70% to pass (Certiport does not publish an official cut score) · valid 2 years · ~150 hours of hands-on Fusion recommended
Delivered by: Certiport (a Pearson VUE business); credential owned by Autodesk
Cost: ~$83 voucher alone; $141 Certiport bundle (voucher + free retake + CertPREP practice); schools usually buy via a Certiport site license — confirm the campus/EPISD route before quoting
Exam domainWhat it covers
1 · Workspace & NavigationData panel, orbit/zoom/pan, ViewCube, browser & toolbar, units/grid/snaps, the Timeline, work planes/axes/points
2 · SketchSketch tools & palette, project geometry, edit (trim/offset/mirror/pattern), text, constraints & dimensions, design parameters -> parametric model
3 · ModelSolids from sketches (extrude/revolve/sweep/loft, holes, threads, patterns); modify (fillet/chamfer/shell/draft/split/combine/press-pull = 'direct modeling'); Forms/sculpt (T-Spline)
4 · AssembleComponents & subassemblies, create component from body, joints (rigid/revolute/slider), drive joints, interference check
5 · DocumentDrawings (views, sheets, title block), dimensions & annotations, balloons, parts list / BOM

Prep resources:

  • Autodesk free self-paced learning for Fusion
  • Autodesk Fusion tutorials hub
  • Certiport - Autodesk certify page (official objectives PDF)
  • Official practice: CertPREP/GMetrix (voucher+retake+practice bundle $141)
  • Free gold standard: Learn Fusion 360 in 30 Days (Product Design Online)
  • Stretch (a level up): Autodesk 'CAD for Mechanical Design' cert-prep course

Coverage note: Coverage: domains 1-4 are hit hard across the bank. Two to reinforce on purpose - Document (5) shows up mainly in #15/#16, so make 'produce a dimensioned drawing' a recurring exit requirement on #3, #6, #9, #11; and Forms/sculpt (3.3) appears mainly in #14, so add a second short Form build if time allows. Every build type you asked for is here: parametric part (#3), knurled bolt & nut (#7), enclosure (#9), phone stand (#8), joint assembly (#11), drawing/BOM (#15), sculpt (#14), multi-body product (#13/#16).

Path to certification

  1. Phase 0 - Basics (prereq) - Learn Fusion 360 in 30 Days (sketch -> extrude -> revolve -> basic edits), or credit prior work (~15-20 days)
  2. Phase 1 - Warm-ups - Projects 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4; end by making a quick drawing of the bracket (seed the Document domain) (~4-5 days)
  3. Phase 2 - Core (manufacturing parts) - Projects 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8 -> 9; add a dimensioned drawing on the bolt and the enclosure (~7-9 days)
  4. Diagnostic checkpoint - First CertPREP/GMetrix practice in Training mode (open-book); use the score report to target weak domains (~1 day)
  5. Phase 3 - Advanced - Projects 10 -> 11 -> 12 -> 13 -> 14 -> 15 (assemblies, motion, forms, drawings) (~12-14 days)
  6. Phase 4 - Capstone - Project 16 (product -> assembly -> drawing), graded across all 5 domains (~4-5 days)
  7. Phase 5 - Cert practice -> exam - Timed CertPREP/GMetrix in Testing mode until consistently ~80%+, then sit the ACU exam (~2-3 days)

Design Notebook - Setup & Table of Contents

Every engineer keeps a design notebook (engineering journal). It holds your notes, sketches, brainstorms, plans, and test data all year. Set it up today - we grade a notebook check each unit.

Set it up (do this now)

  1. Cover: your name, class, and period on the front.
  2. Pages 1-3: leave blank and label them "Table of Contents."
  3. Number every page (bottom corner).
  4. Date every entry. New day = new dated heading.
  5. Never tear pages out. Cross out mistakes with one line - engineers keep their thinking.

Table of Contents (start it)
